items.title: Lisa came to China for a better life, but was 'auctioned off' for marriage
items.description: The ABC has spoken to multiple Tongan women who have been lured into an arranged marriage syndicate operating in China, with allegations of passports being confiscated and tens of thousands of dollars changing hands.

items.title: The 'fairy gold dust passport' more Australians are chasing
items.description: Australians are racing to secure Irish citizenship, with new figures showing applications have more than doubled in the past three years as people seek the right to live, work and study across the EU.

items.title: Visa refusal may prevent ex-ASIO source giving Bondi evidence
items.description: The man who previously warned ASIO about the Bondi gunmen won't be able to give sensitive and classified evidence at the Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

items.title: 'Nervous' investors retreat from housing market as downturn broadens
items.description: Australia's property market has entered a downturn after both house and unit prices fell for the first time in more than three years, bringing an end to the recent housing boom.

items.title: Inside CPAC London: Charlatans, conspiracy theories and loud snoring
items.description: In 10 years at the ABC, I've had some strange experiences. I can now add last week's CPAC conference in London to the list, and it's going somewhere near the top, says Riley Stuart in London.

items.title: China demands Australia stop 'inciting confrontation' over South China Sea
items.description: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has demanded Australia stop "exaggerating tensions and inciting confrontation" over the South China Sea after Penny Wong warned Beijing against "destabilising" conduct in the region.

items.title: How we got to Glasgow 2026 and what the Commonwealth Games will look like
items.description: The bumpy road to Glasgow 2026 has produced a Commonwealth Games that will look a little different than the ones that came before.

items.title: Labor conference to debate gas and gambling
items.description: Anthony Albanese may have been a keen participant in robust conference debates in years gone by but is now using his authority to enforce a much more controlled process.

items.title: French modelling scout with links to Epstein found dead, prosecutors say
items.description: A French modelling scout with close ties to the late US financier Jeffrey Epstein has been found dead at his home outside Paris, prosecutors say.

items.title: Meet the Australian multi-millionaire pardoned by Trump
items.description: Chris Wade was arrested by the Secret Service in Dallas in the early 2000s. It took him on a journey where he went from FBI hacker to Mar-a-Lago and eventually the White House before he came back to Australia to buy his favourite pub.

items.title: How One Nation's winning over the bush
items.description: One Nation has some of its strongest support in outback Australia and recent polling shows it could win over 30 regional seats. So what's winning over regional Australians when it comes to Pauline Hanson's party?

items.title: US and Saudi Arabia set to unveil nuclear power deal, media reports say
items.description: Israeli officials and US politicians from both parties have voiced concern that a civilian nuclear project in Saudi Arabia could be converted to eventually develop nuclear weapons.

items.title: Trump threatens Iranian power plants, bridges if ships attacked in Hormuz
items.description: US strikes have already widened from the south to western and central areas of Iran in recent days.

items.title: Minister says Australian IS-linked 'Doctor Jihad' can 'rot' in Iraqi jail
items.description: Perth paediatrician Tareq Kamleh went to Syria to join the Islamic State group in 2015 and has, until now, been presumed dead.

items.title: How Nintendo's tariff hike ended with angry gamers and a lawsuit
items.description: Nintendo has argued it has no duty to pass its refunds onto US consumers. It's the latest in a lengthy tariff fight.

items.title: You reckon you know the Logies? Try our quiz
items.description: As the Logies approach, on August 16, we thought we would test your knowledge of the beloved but daggy Australian television awards and this year's nominees.

items.title: The nefarious rise of Putin is skewered in this satirical drama
items.description: Cannes darling Oliver Assayas tackles the shadowy forces of our time in his latest film, The Wizard of the Kremlin.

items.title: 'Unheard and uncared for': Children in state care exploited by adults
items.description: The ABC has spoken with experts, advocates and residential care workers as part of a 19-month investigation into the sexual exploitation of children in state care.

items.title: 'Grave concern' as Wagga Wagga's homeless threatened with $1,100 fines
items.description: Homeless advocates are slamming the approach of a regional council after it threatened to fine people sleeping rough if they did not move on.

items.title: Data company urged to be 'good' after water plan slip reveals intentions
items.description: A Tasmanian farmer has urged a data centre builder to "be a good corporate citizen" after it accidentally revealed a plan to tap into a water source earmarked for agriculture for cooling purposes at one of its facilities.

items.title: Anxiety as Australia issues new travel advice for Middle East countries
items.description: As conflict between the United States and Iran escalates once again, the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has issued a warning to "reconsider" travel to several more countries in the region.

items.title: Court date set for trial of captured Venezuelan president Maduro
items.description: US commandos captured Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores in January this year and took them to New York, where they now face a number of charges including narcoterrorism.

items.title: Hanson labels domestic violence 'two-way street'
items.description: The One Nation leader says women should not "put up with" domestic violence, as she highlights the cost-of-living pressures on families.

items.title: Rural suburb flagged as home for proposed $40b 'hyperscale' data centre
items.description: A proposed massive new data centre would require more than six times the total demand of the Darwin and Katherine electricity grids to operate and be powered by gas piped direct from the Northern Territory's Beetaloo Basin.

items.title: Ukraine hits more warehouses of top Russian retailer Wildberries
items.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv struck "logistics hubs" supplying the Russian army with "drone components, navigation equipment and other gear".
